channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Alberta minister says Ottawa's nicotine pouch regulations abandon rural communities
item.description: Rural communities experience nicotine policy differently. A rule that looks manageable in urban centres can become a serious access barrier where pharmacies, services and cessation support are limited. Ottawa’s pouch regulations raise that equity question: are lower-risk options being placed out of reach for the people who may have the fewest alternatives? Harm reduction should not depend on postcode, political visibility or proximity to the right kind of retailer. (Published on September 25, 2026bywesternstandard.news)

item.title: The People Missing From Australia’s Tobacco-Control Victory
item.description: Australia’s nicotine debate often talks about systems, markets and enforcement, but the people most affected can disappear from view. Smokers who cannot quit, vapers pushed into prescription workarounds, and consumers navigating illicit supply are not footnotes to policy — they are the evidence of how policy works in practice. A strategy that ignores them may look tidy from above while failing on the ground. Public health should count lived experience as part of the evidence, not as an inconvenience to the model. (Published on September 25, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: U.S. Regulators Plan Major Move to Speed Authorizations of Vapes, Tobacco Pouches
item.description: A faster FDA pathway for vapes and nicotine pouches would matter most for the legal market. Years of slow authorisations have left adult smokers with limited approved options while illicit and unapproved products fill the gap. Speed should not mean weak standards; it should mean timely, evidence-based decisions that distinguish responsible smoke-free products from those that fail basic tests. Harm reduction needs regulation that can move quickly enough to keep safer alternatives inside accountable channels. (Published on September 25, 2026bywsj.com)
